name: Agent Checkpoints
description: An agent's run as a line of checkpoints, like git for agents – rewind to any of them and a new attempt branches out of it, while the one it left fades back but stays

name: Agent Cursors
description: Agents working in a document like teammates in a multiplayer editor – live pointers with names, suggestions typed letter by letter, images they resize, code they fix and comments beside the page

name: Agent Findings
description: A swarm of agents checking something – one calm row per agent with its progress, and their findings sliding into a short feed as they're found

name: Agent Fleet
description: Several agents side by side – each card sums up its sub-agents, and a click opens its tree to the right while the last one folds back into its card

name: Agent Graph
description: Agents and the tools they call as a living network – a pulse along the link for every call and its answer, busy links growing thicker, agents that breathe while they work and turn amber when they need you

name: Agent Handoff
description: A task passed from agent to agent like a relay – at every handoff what went along to the next one, and what got lost on the way

name: Agent Inbox
description: Background tasks in a Board or List, grouped by Needs you, Running, and Done. Expand cards to review steps, approve, reject, or retry.

name: Agent Lanes
description: Where every agent is right now – a live timeline with a lane per agent, tasks growing into “now”, hand-offs drawn between agents and approvals right on the block

name: Agent Ledger
description: Everything an agent changed in your systems, each change with an undo – before and after per row, and pointing at Undo shows what builds on it: what would be undone too, and what can't be taken back

name: Agent Monitor
description: One agent at work, as a card – its current step with a clock and the bill so far, a time strip and the finished steps with the logo of each tool, a click on any of them for the details; the exact command when it needs your OK; folds into a small bar with the tools it has used

name: Agent Plan
description: An agent's step-by-step plan to review before it runs – rename, drag to reorder, remove or add steps, then watch each one run with live timers and retry from a failed step

name: Agent Queue
description: The work waiting for your agents, and how fast it moves – jobs drop into a live queue, glide into free worker slots as growing bars and land in Done or Failed, while a depth chart shows the backlog build up when a rate limit pauses the workers and drain when they resume

name: Agent Recap
description: What the agents did while you were away – the night as a small chart with a peak per event, then a board of what needs you, what failed and what's done, acted on right on the card

name: Agent Steering
description: Steer an agent while it works – queue a note for the next step and watch it glide into the plan when the agent picks it up, or interrupt right away

name: Agent Trail
description: The steps an agent works through, as one quiet trail – a header with the task and "3/5", done ones with a check and their time, the one it is on says what it is doing and branches into its sub-steps with a live timer, a step that needs approval waits with a dashed ring; a short fading light runs down the trail into the sub-step it is on

name: Agent Tree
description: Who started whom – an orchestrator and its sub-agents as a live tree, with status, cost and time on every card, costs rolling up each branch, and branches that fold to one line

name: AI Answer
description: Streamed answer with source cards, citation chips that preview their source, copy, regenerate, feedback and follow-ups

name: Approval Card
description: An agent asks before it acts – risk badge, preview, Approve and Deny with shortcuts, a pausing countdown, and a smooth morph into a resolved row

name: Approval Gates
description: The approval requests of an agent run as a stack of cards – the one to decide now on top with who asks, what exactly and why, the diff or arguments on it; approve, reject or change it first, and it drops into the decided list while the next rises – open ones hold the steps behind them

name: Autonomy Dial
description: How much an agent may do on its own – a three-stop dial, and its real actions gliding between “Runs on its own” and “Asks you first”, with a lock for what always asks

name: Away Summary
description: The “While you were away” card for a chat thread – right where you left off: how long you were gone, what needs you, what failed and what's done as a short list with one action per row; Got it folds it into a one-line divider

name: Billing Schedule
description: Build a billing phase – start date, duration, products with repeats and timing, discount, minimum and live totals

name: Breakdown Chart
description: Stacked bar chart with measure, slice and segment pickers, a hover breakdown and a linked table

name: Button
description: Primary, secondary, ghost and destructive buttons with icons, sizes and a shimmering loading state

name: Change Summary
description: What moved since last time – one metric per row with a colored trend

name: Chat Composer
description: Prompt composer with model picker, voice input, app connections and approval request

name: Checkbox
description: A real checkbox with a label and a second line, a some-of-them state for Select all, an error and a card row – the check draws itself

name: Cited Answer
description: An AI answer wired to its sources – point at a citation to light up its sentence and source, click to unfold the quoted passage with the matching words marked

name: Collaboration Stream
description: What agents actually say to each other – a quiet chat where every message shows who it is from and who it is for, handoffs and questions for you tagged, files as chips that open a preview, a card with details under every message, and a composer to name agents with @ or answer a question

name: Combobox
description: Pick one or many from a searchable, grouped list – chips with avatars, highlighted matches, create-on-the-fly and full keyboard support

name: Command Menu
description: Search and run anything from one field – tool actions with logos and ⌘1–⌘5, everyday commands with icons

name: Comment Thread
description: One comment with replies – an assistant reports what it did, folds open details and answers @mentions

name: Comments Panel
description: Comment feed with filters, runnable /edit commands, resolve and a composer

name: Compact Breakdown
description: A total split into its parts in one small card – numbers roll, the bar glides and the ranked rows trade places when the period changes

name: Conflict Radar
description: Agents working on their own branches at once, and where they get in each other's way – a row per file and a column per agent, a line between the agents that changed the same lines, each agent's way in one sentence to pick from, and Merge once all are settled

name: Context Map
description: What fills an agent's context window, as a living treemap – system prompt, tools, memory, every file, the chat and tool results as tiles that glide as it grows, the free space dashed, and compaction squeezing old turns into a summary

name: Context Window
description: What fills the model's context, as a field of cells – hover a part to light it up, remove files, and compact the conversation while its cells shimmer and clear

name: Cost Waterfall
description: Where the money and tokens of an agent run go – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a step in a waterfall, with model, tokens, cost and time, the most expensive step on top and a switch between cost and tokens

name: Data Table
description: Spreadsheet-style table: select cells and ranges, edit in place, copy and paste, undo and sort

name: Date Range Picker
description: Presets and two calendars with a hover preview, comparison with the previous period or year, full keyboard control

name: Decision Card
description: An agent's question, asked the way Claude asks one – its own card just above the chat composer: numbered options with one Recommended, Approve / Decline for an approval, preview tiles for a pick, and a last row for your own words; a click or 1–5 answers, Later folds it to one line

name: Decision Inbox
description: Open decisions with two quick answers each – answered ones confirm and fold away

name: Decision Tree
description: An agent stuck on a decision lays out its options as a tree – the consequences of each branch, the risky ones marked, its own pick highlighted – and you choose a path or write your own

name: Delegate Board
description: Hand work to your agents by dragging it onto them – each agent previews its new “busy until” time, or switch to Auto and every new task goes to whoever is free first

name: Dropzone
description: Drag files in and watch them upload – fanning documents, colored type badges, progress with time left, errors with retry

name: Email Draft
description: Agent-written email for review – switch recipient and tone, edit inline, remove the attachment, send or discard with undo

name: Experiment Card
description: An A/B test in two lines that quietly unfolds on hover – variants linked to a tiny chart, a metric switch with rolling numbers, and a winner you pick with a click

name: Fallback Chain
description: One request finding a model that answers, as a small flow diagram – the request branches out to each model in its fallback order, a light runs to the one being tried, failed branches break red, and the one that answers runs on to the response

name: Fan-out Grid
description: One agent hands a big job to many workers – every task a cell on a live grid that fills in as they get through it, with retries, failures, cost and the time left, and the details of any task on hover

name: Filter Menu
description: Grouped filters with removable chips, collapsible checkbox groups, Clear all and full keyboard control

name: Inline Diff
description: AI edits to prose shown inline – struck and added words you accept or reject one by one, with keys, a popover and undo

name: Integration Picker
description: Integrations page of a command menu – search, a list of services and the picked one with its connection on two tiles

name: Integration Settings
description: Settings card for a connected service – on/off switch, API key, validated site address, time zone and a save bar

name: Judge Bracket
description: How an LLM judge picks the best of several attempts, as a tournament – two answers at a time, the one it prefers moves on, the other fades back; the winner's way through the bracket lights up, and every match opens both answers side by side with the scores and why

name: KPI Chart
description: Metric card with a multi-line chart and a tooltip that follows the pointer

name: Memory Panel
description: What the assistant remembers about you, grouped and editable – a master switch, category filters, and on every memory edit in place, pause or forget with Undo on the tray

name: Message Actions
description: The quiet bar under an AI message – copy turns into a check, regenerate spins and unfolds a version switcher, thumbs pop and ask why, read aloud becomes a tiny equalizer

name: Model Picker
description: The model menu of an AI chat – point at a model and its speed, quality and cost bars fill, switch on extended thinking and its effort unfolds, while the tray rolls the first-token time and price

name: Notification Stack
description: Notice cards stacked behind each other – dismiss the front one to reveal the next

name: OTP Input
description: The verification code field done right – a gliding focus ring, paste and SMS autofill, a calm shake on errors and a morph into Verified

name: Parallel Attempts
description: An agent tries the same task several ways at once and the best one wins – every attempt races as a row with its model, approach and live bar, then gets a score; the best is marked and picked, and you can switch to another

name: Permission Request
description: An agent asks for one specific right – who, why and exactly what will happen – and you allow it once, for an hour or always; then it folds into one line with the time left and Revoke

name: Plan vs Actual
description: An agent's plan against what really happens – every step's bar grows over its dashed planned ghost, overruns turn amber, the steps after it slide right, and the expected finish moves away from the planned one

name: Profile Menu
description: Account card with the signed-in user, menu actions and profile setup progress

name: Progress Tracker
description: Onboarding checklist with an animated progress bar, ticks that draw themselves and auto play

name: Project Card
description: A two-line project summary that quietly unfolds on hover – a progress ring with one segment per subtask, a people filter and a status picker, all linked by hover

name: Prompt Library
description: Saved prompt templates with variables – type straight into the sentence, watch the finished prompt assemble below, and use it once every variable is filled

name: Reaction Bar
description: Like, comment, repost and share in one pill – icons pop and fill, counts roll in digit by digit

name: Review Center
description: A focused workspace for what your agents want to do – the queue sorted by risk, one item at a time with the shaky spans marked, Approve, Edit, Reject and Skip on single keys, a stamp as each one leaves and the next one rising in

name: Root Cause Tree
description: How an agent finds out why a run failed, as a fault tree – it checks one hypothesis after another, rules some out, confirms the cause, and the way up to the failure lights up

name: Running Now
description: A live status of background agent tasks for a header or sidebar – one quiet pill, "3 running · 2 need you"; open it for the tasks with a filling ring, the step each is on and its steps, Pause and Resume, and Open on the ones that wait for you

name: Scheduled Runs
description: Agent tasks sorted into a week of sessions – each session has a usage limit, small tasks fill the gaps, big ones are split across sessions, and the stack flies in one card at a time

name: Segmented Control
description: Switch between two to six options – a raised pill or underline that glides, stretches a little and can be dragged across, with icons, counts and badges

name: Select
description: Pick one option in the Text Field's look – icons and a second line per option, a gliding highlight, type-ahead and a list that never gets cut off

name: Setup Guide
description: Onboarding panel with a progress bar and collapsible task groups that strike through when done

name: Smart Recommendation
description: Suggestion card with a confidence signal, alternatives to switch to and accept with undo

name: Stepper Form
description: A multi-step flow for onboarding and setup – steps that fill and check off, sliding steps, a card that morphs to each step, inline validation and a success state

name: Switch
description: On or off for things that apply right away – label and second line, at the start or across a settings row, a thumb that stretches as you press it

name: Tag Input
description: Several values in one field as chips – paste a whole list, a check per value, duplicates flash, Backspace and arrow keys to edit

name: Text Area
description: The multi-line twin of the Text Field – grows with the text, a character count, a button for more room and ⌘ Enter to send

name: Text Field
description: One input for every form – label, hint and error in place, prefix and suffix, clear, show-password and copy buttons, a character count

name: Thinking Loader
description: A small working pill for AI replies – an eight-ray spinner and a shimmering label that rolls through phases and settles on a check

name: Thinking State
description: AI working panel with a live timer, searched sources and thinking steps that appear one by one
usage:
import Example from "./thinking-state";
export default function App() { return <Example />; }

name: Tips Panel
description: Grid of short tips with one action each – taken tips turn into a done state

name: Toaster
description: Calm toasts from anywhere – a stack that fans out on hover, promise toasts that morph from spinner to check, swipe to dismiss

name: Tool Access Map
description: An agent in the middle with every tool it can reach around it – which ones it used, which failed and which it calls right now; open a tool for its calls and replay one on its own

name: Tool Call Card
description: An agent's tool call in one line – live timer, status and summary, folds open to highlighted arguments and result with copy, retry on errors and a group that sums them up

name: Trace Waterfall
description: Where the time and money of an agent run go – every LLM call, tool call and sub-agent as a bar on a live timeline, with tokens and cost per step, the slowest call marked and branches that fold into their parent

name: Usage Meter
description: Plan usage and AI credits – a stacked credits meter by category, daily sparkline, limits and a button that speaks up near the limit

name: Writing Assistant
description: AI chat card with a soft gradient glow, suggestions, streaming replies and live voice dictation
